data.body:
RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 complete) — proven root cause + attribution

MECHANISM (runtime-confirmed): sign_manifest's generation loop
(src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:289-291) treats a transient
`store-read-failure` from the pre-lock reads (tracker_head_sha / collect) as
TERMINAL — it immediately `raise PlanReviewGenerationError(exc.reason)`. The
sibling transient just below (moving committed HEAD, `before != after`,
line 292) is instead RETRIED via `continue`, and after MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS
exhaustion raises the *retryable* PlanReviewGenerationRetryable. The two are the
same class of concurrency artifact, handled asymmetrically.

WHY store-read-failure fires under concurrency: rebar's ticket-event write path
stages tracked entries with `git add` then `git commit` (event_append.py:155
"lock, atomic-rename, git add+commit"; event_commit_git.py:99 `git add`) on the
ONE shared .git/index every session symlinks. The signing preflight reads
(before/collect/after) run `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` and
`git ls-files -u` (relation_snapshot.py:104) WITHOUT holding the store write
lock, so they can observe a peer session mid add->commit: a staged tracked entry
-> non-empty status -> store-read-failure. Rate scales with concurrency, matching
the observed symptom (repeated PASS-but-signing-aborted while several sessions ran).

RUNTIME PROOF (isolated temp repo, deterministic):
  CASE 1 clean                        -> tracker_head_sha OK (== HEAD)
  CASE 2 untracked .tmp-event present -> ignore_untracked=True OK; =False RAISES
                                         (d7cb-22ae fixed exactly this untracked half)
  CASE 3 STAGED tracked entry         -> ignore_untracked=True RAISES store-read-failure
CASE 3 is the mechanism: untracked-ignoring does NOT save the staged-index window.

DEFECT LEGITIMACY: defect. Authoritative source = the design invariant that
signing must tolerate the NORMAL transient state of many concurrent sessions on
one shared tracker (stated in resign.py:160-200 and partially enforced by
d7cb-22ae). The staged-index variant is the same contract, unmet; and the loop's
own retry of the sibling moving-HEAD transient is the local contract this handler
violates. Not-a-bug guard cleared.

ATTRIBUTION: origin commit 94e605a29d2 "Add phased plan-review attestations"
(ticket 5967-4476-7f9f-442d) introduced the asymmetric handler (blame of
generation.py:289-291). d7cb-22ae (1475e2868de) is a carrier/partial-fix: it added
ignore_untracked=True (fixing the untracked trigger) but left the terminal raise
in place, so the staged-window trigger survived. Date test: the terminal-on-
transient behavior has existed since 94e605 (the feature's introduction), so the
origin is 94e605 / 5967, not the later partial fix. Class: plan_defect (the
attestation feature's plan omitted concurrency-robust handling of the transient
store-read-failure).

FIX DIRECTION (Phase 2): make a transient store-read-failure retryable within the
existing MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS loop (continue, mirroring the moving-HEAD path;
raise PlanReviewGenerationRetryable only after exhaustion) so a peer's in-flight
staged index no longer aborts signing. The authoritative under-lock re-check
(under_lock_check, run while holding the store write lock so no writer can be mid
add->commit) remains the fence, so retrying the pre-lock reads is safe.
